stories.score_hints: Biggest story of the day, every outlet covers it; reference accounts covered it on 11-12 (ai.trend.kr, moodmode.ai 3.1x). Korea/Asia angle exists (Korea Times, Korea Herald, Yonhap on Seoul shares) but those originals were not readable. Same-company note: Nvidia appeared in 11-07 and 11-09 posts, different stories.

articles.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
Five ways Jensen Huang's ouster from Nvidia could damage the AI industry
Jensen Huang's exit puts Nvidia's support for open source in question

facts.fact: Nvidia confirmed in an SEC filing on Thursday that the board accepted Huang's resignation on Wednesday.
CFO Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties; Nvidia is expected to run a larger search for a permanent successor.
Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as Nvidia's first-ever chair of the board.

U.S. officials believe Megaspeed executive Alice Huang (no relation), a Chinese citizen, is a Chinese spy; Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly bought $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over two years.
In a letter to employees on November 8 Huang wrote: "I was unfaithful to my wife." Nvidia's board started an independent investigation.
Huang agreed to testify in Congress before Thanksgiving (November 26); the testimony is expected to be behind closed doors.

Huang co-founded Nvidia 33 years ago; Nvidia stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and was down 11% over five days. He has about 60 direct reports and the company had no obvious succession plan.
Nvidia has agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $13 billion (the deal is not yet finalized); Huang was the loudest advocate of open-weight AI models.
An Nvidia insider told TechCrunch they do not expect a leadership change to affect development of the Nemotron open-weight models.

stories.title: US readies rules to block China's remote use of Nvidia GPUs in 7 countries, as Chinese firms rush to lock in capacity
stories.score_hints: Follow-on of the Huang story (export controls); same company as pick 1, so choose one. Fact source is AI Times Korea citing The Information and Reuters (Korean, translated by researcher).

articles.title: 미국, 중국의 해외 GPU 임대 규제 추진…중국 기업들 확보 서둘러

facts.fact: The Information reported on the 11th (US time), citing two people, that the US Commerce Department is finalizing a rule limiting remote access by Chinese AI companies to overseas data centers; it could be announced as early as this month.

The rule would tighten export controls on advanced AI chips to 7 countries: Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Brazil, Norway and South Africa; Nvidia Blackwell and later chips would need a US license.
Data center operators in those countries would have to report who receives the chips and what they are used for to Commerce, and be monitored on an ongoing basis.

Reuters reported on the 12th, citing three people, that Chinese AI companies are trying to secure overseas Nvidia GPU capacity before the rule takes effect; one large Chinese cloud company discussed reserving capacity in advance.
The Remote Access Security Act passed the House in January and awaits Senate review.
Nvidia said in July that the act could significantly affect its business; The Information said the rule may show Nvidia's influence in Washington is weakening.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster Flash-tier model, in Search, the Gemini app and the API
stories.score_hints: Big launch with hard numbers; no reference account covered it yet (they covered Claude/Higgsfield). Original is Google's own announcement (company claims, benchmark numbers are Google's).

facts.fact: Google introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen on Nov 12, 2026, built for rapid execution in everyday coding and agentic workflows; the frontier models are Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon.
Hydrogen is priced flat across its 1 million-token context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.
Google says Hydrogen scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level vs 50 for Argon, reaching 54 at the highest xhigh setting.
Versus Gemini 3.8 Flash, Google says Hydrogen finishes tasks 2.5 times faster at its default setting and scores 57% vs 18.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1.
It is available in Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app and Google Search; paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers get it in Google Antigravity.
In Search, Google says it better understands multi-part questions, gives more visual answers and widens the range of links via an upgraded query fan-out.

Google introduced Orchestrator in Antigravity, which switches between models such as Carbon and Hydrogen in one session; on Terminal-Bench 4.0 it used on average 24% less quota and finished 19% faster.

facts.fact: Google unveiled a Gemini-based 'Intelligent Eyewear' line made with Samsung, Gentle Monster and Warby Parker; pre-orders began Nov 12 (US time) in Korea and the US.
Official launch date is Dec 10; the Gentle Monster collection sells in Korea and the US, the Warby Parker collection only in the US.
The glasses have no AR display; they work through voice commands and visual recognition, and are compatible with Galaxy phones and iPhones.
They have a 12-megapixel ultra-wide camera and open speakers, weigh about 41 g, and last up to 9 hours on battery.
US starting prices: Gentle Monster $449 (about 600,000 won), Warby Parker $395 (about 530,000 won).
Gemini automatically blurs bystanders' faces before processing video, and recording stops if the indicator light is covered or tampered with; a physical switch turns power fully off.
Omdia says Meta had 85.2% of global AI smart glasses shipments last year and 81.3% in the first half of this year; Omdia expects over 15 million AI glasses shipped this year.

stories.title: SpaceX announces more than $74 billion for AI campuses in Texas and Arizona, including a 6 GW site
stories.score_hints: Hard numbers ($74B, 6 GW, 2,400 petition signatures against). Reuters headline in feeds but readable original is AI Times Korea (cites Reuters).

articles.title: 스페이스X, 100조 규모 AI 데이터센터 투자…애리조나에 6GW 추가

facts.fact: SpaceX officially announced on Nov 12 (US time) over $74 billion (about 100 trillion won) for AI supercomputing facilities in Texas and Arizona.

Arizona: $50 billion for an AI campus using up to 6 GW of power, on a 747-acre site in Cochise County with up to 9 data center buildings, built in four 1.5 GW phases; construction could start March 2027 if local approval is given.

Texas: more than $24 billion near Starbase for a data center and natural gas power plant that generates its own power instead of using the public grid; Starbase city council reviews a property-tax break on Dec 9.
SpaceX claims co-op members' electricity bills could fall by up to 20%, and says it will use dry cooling and no industrial groundwater.
About 2,400 people signed a petition against the Arizona permit; Cochise County holds a hearing in December.
Arizona is expected to create 5,500 construction jobs and 1,000 operating jobs.
Per Reuters, AI business made up more than half of SpaceX's Q3 revenue.

articles.title: OpenAI revenue hits $10bn a quarter as its adjusted losses widen
Datum offiziell: Anthropic-Aktien ab 19. November im Handel

facts.fact: OpenAI's Q3 revenue reached $10bn, up almost 50% from Q2 and almost three times a year earlier, per The Information and Bloomberg as cited by TNW.
Adjusted operating loss rose to $10.9bn from $10.1bn, while adjusted operating margin improved to -109% from -150% (WSJ).
OpenAI ended September with roughly $50bn in annualised revenue.
Anthropic reported $16.96bn revenue for the same quarter, with an operating loss of $567m and 15% adjusted operating margin; growth was about 47% vs 144% the quarter before.
The two count revenue differently: Anthropic includes sales through cloud partners, OpenAI counts only its share of some partner sales.
OpenAI is completing a funding round at a $1.25tn valuation and has delayed its listing until next year.
Anthropic shares are to start trading Nov 19 if approved; final price set around Nov 18; indicated range $70-$78 per share; up to about 801 million shares and up to about $64 billion gross proceeds.

articles.title: Anthropic lets companies run Claude's agent service on their own servers

facts.fact: Anthropic now lets companies run Claude Managed Agents in their own cloud account or data centre; launched Thursday, access by request through the Anthropic account team.
Agents, session histories and credentials stay on the customer's systems and every tool call can be logged.
Each time the agent asks Claude something, the conversation still goes to a model provider such as Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud or Microsoft Foundry.
Customers take on securing and updating the server; nothing migrates from the hosted service, and webhooks and scheduled runs are missing.
TNW notes ECB president Christine Lagarde has warned of the risk of relying on foreign AI, and Mistral has pitched sovereign AI.
OpenAI took a different route in September, letting companies run its agents inside Amazon's cloud.

articles.title: United Airlines blocks AI agents from booking flights, citing cybersecurity risks

facts.fact: United will restrict access for AI agents that book flights and manage reservations for users, citing cybersecurity risk and federal regulations.
United warns that sharing credentials with third-party AI assistants can expose sensitive information and lead to unintended purchases, account changes or use of MileagePlus miles.
Federal aviation rules require a human to complete flight check-in to acknowledge bags hold no banned substances.
United will restrict access directly on its platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators, updating booking, ticketing and distribution policies.
Last week banks including Bank of America urged customers not to share passwords with AI assistants.
